title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: interpreters vitam; Zanchius/Pareus; sanctitas as sanitas
pass_a_gloss: And so all the interpreters I have seen rendered life, not lives, and either sought no mystery in the plural חַיִּים, or thought there were hinted by it those lives which are absolutely necessary to man's essence and nature—vegetative, sensitive, and rational—which opinion of Zanchius and Pareus is not to be despised: for as the formation of the Body, so also this inspiration of נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים pertained to man's fabrication and composition and constitution, to which I gladly also refer sanctity and blessedness, increased by Adam's introduction into paradise after he was created. For sanctity stood to the soul as health to the body.
pass_b_english: So every interpreter I have seen rendered "life," not "lives." Either they found no mystery in the plural חַיִּים, or they took it to hint at the lives strictly needed for human essence and nature—vegetative, sensitive, and rational—which is Zanchius's and Pareus's view, and not to be scorned.

As the body's formation belonged to making and composing the human being, so did this inspiring of נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים. To that same constitution I gladly also refer sanctity and blessedness, increased when Adam, after he was made, was brought into paradise. Sanctity stood to the soul as health stands to the body.
source_text: Itaque interpretes omnes quos viderim, vitam verterunt non vitas, & vel nihil mysterii in plurali חַיִּים quaesierunt, vel putarunt eo innui eas vitas, quae ad hominis essentiam & naturam sunt absolute necessariae, vegetativam, sensitivam, & rationalem, quae Zanchii & Parei opinio est non contemnenda: quam enim formatio Corporis, tam haec quoque נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים inspiratio ad hominis fabricationem & compositionem, ac constitutionem pertinebat, ad quam etiam sanctitatem & beatitudinem, introductione Adami, postquam creatus fuit, in paradisum, auctam, libenter refero. Habebat enim se sanctitas ad animam, ut sanitas ad corpus.

choices.choice: Keep vitam rendering; allow Zanchius/Pareus faculty reading; sanctitas~sanitas
